newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia says rabbit virus results are good.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia says rabbit virus results are good.

text.p: A recently-released virus to cut Australia's pest rabbit population had killed up to 95 percent of rabbits in some areas, Primary Industies Minister John Anderson said on Wednesday.
Anderson said data from 10 monitoring sites across Australia showed 80 to 95 percent of rabbits had been killed within six to eight weeks of the release of the rabbit calicivirus.
The virus had been released at 181 areas across mainland Australia in the two months since it was declared a biological control agent against rabbits, he said.

"Reports from the field indicate the impact of the virus on the wild rabbit population has already significantly enhanced prospects for long-term sustainability of millions of hectares of rabbit-prone country," Anderson said in a statement.
But he said the disease was still patchy in some areas.
"The slow spread in certain areas means it will be some months before the full impact is realised," he said.

Farmers blame rabbits -- imported by a British hunting enthusiast in the 19th century -- for causing hundreds of millions of dollars of damage to crops and for driving indigenous animals and plants to the verge of extinction.
The virus is ultimately expected to be released at a total of 280 sites in all of Australia's six states and two territories.
